text:
Rowan: Small holiday PSA: someone left an impressively large gingerbread house in the kitchen overnight. Its now a gingerbread crime scene — our office cat (Rolo?) may have adopted it. Photo attached. :house_with_garden: :cat2:
Priya: NOOO poor house. Also Rolo is iconic. Who left the architectural masterpiece?
Rowan: No note on it. I put a sticky: 'investigation pending, do not demolish (again)'. I moved the broken pieces to a plate to avoid more casualties.
Mateo: This is the kind of chaos I live for. Ill bring a tiny icing repair kit at 3pm and we can attempt a structural emergency patch. Anyone want to join the gingerbread forensics team? :whisk:
Zoe: Im in. Also mandatory festive playlist for the repair crew? I vote for something aggressively cheerful.
Carmen: Count me in too. Quick thought: can we set a "Gingerbread Adoption" rule? If you build it, leave a care note with allergens and whether Rolo is allowed to inspect.
Rowan: Love it. Also shoutout to Facilities for leaving extra folding chairs in the kitchen last week  they saved our repair seating. :clap:
holiday-bot: Reminder scheduled: Thu 15:00 in #random  "Gingerbread house triage & cookie diplomacy" :white_check_mark:
Priya: Tiny poll: should we keep the rebuilt house in the kitchen all week (and risk Rolos curiosity) or create a decorative display on the top shelf (Rolo-proof)? React :one: for kitchen, :two: for shelf.
Mateo: Reacted :two: for shelf. Also bringing spare sprinkles and hot cocoa as bribe materials.
Zoe: Shelf seems safer. Rolo is a specialist in targeting seasonal baked goods.
Carmen: If we preserve it on the shelf, can we label it with a silly plaque like "Office Landmark: Do Not Pet (or eat)"?
Rowan: Plaque approved. Also huge thanks everyone for the rescue offers. Holiday vibes + tiny teamwork = perfect. Happy almost-holidays! :sparkles: :cookie:
